goal: The re-driver never transitions a lifecycle by forging an agent claim or status (re-eligibility flows only through sanctioned store/claim APIs), every automatic re-drive/escalate/land path is bounded, and all routed kinds are listable from one queue read.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py -- _recover_claimable_stranded (~460-502): the sanctioned re-eligibility pattern (acquire claim -> finalize_stranded_lifecycle -> release) the re-driver paths must follow rather than writing a status
references: .flywheel/specs/00069-FEATURE-work-redriver.md -- criteria #12 (single surface), #13 (boundedness across all paths), #14 (transition discipline)
constraints: Assert across the re-drive paths (#3, #5, #9 and the land loop): for a never-clearing cause the count of automatic attempts equals the configured bound and a queue entry is produced -- proving no path loops unbounded (criterion #13)

Assert a single queue read returns one unit of each routed kind (#4, #6, #8, #9, #10, #11), each with a distinct machine-readable reason, and that the surface is the existing event/status ledger -- no new silo table (criterion #12)
Assert (grep/AST + green purity tests) that the re-driver paths route through the existing claim/finalize/store APIs rather than writing a status or synthesizing an agent envelope (criterion #14)
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done
non_goals: Do not modify files under packages/*/tests/; do not weaken or delete assertions
Do not relax core purity to make a check pass; do not introduce a new queue silo
edge_cases: If any single re-drive path can exceed its bound, the boundedness assertion must fail -- this is the central anti-goal guard
If routed kinds are scattered across more than one surface, the single-read assertion must fail
